routines.semantics: raw.brcktd(value,end1,end2) returns the value constrained to the closed interval between either ordering of the endpoints. An interior or boundary value remains unchanged; an outside value yields the nearer endpoint. All three inputs must be finite numbers. Actual CSPICE selection, including signed zero, is retained; no alternate JS clamp is used.

scenarios.observes: Observe values below, at both boundaries, inside and above an ordered closed interval.
Repeat the full interval positions with reversed endpoints, distinguishing endpoint-order assumptions.
Observe values below, equal to and above identical endpoints; every result is that endpoint.
Observe exact selected or accumulated finite extrema, including maximum magnitudes and the minimum subnormal; focused live equality prevents ordinary absolute tolerance accepting tiny output as zero.
Observe noninteger values and bounds to distinguish real-valued bracketing from integer conversion.

routines.edgeAssessment: Ordered/reversed/collapsed bounds, finite extrema, subnormals and fractional values are registered. Focused exact live extrema and tagged negative-zero input/output observations strengthen selection semantics.
routines.errorAssessment: NAIF documents this routine as error-free for its defined input domain; no fabricated scientific SPICE error is claimed. Input-type/count/range checks are explicit wrapper safety, with actual valid-call recovery.
routines.fixtureRationale: Authored scalar/array and unit-string inputs only. No kernel, external scientific dataset, file or handle fixture is needed. Independent ctypes bindings load the exact locked SpiceyPy library, not a tspice artifact.
routines.cleanup: Kernel-free authored inputs require no files, data fixtures, handles or retained scientific state. The shared shim uses local result storage and publishes the actual result after SPICE status checking; failures collect diagnostics and reset before throwing. WASM withAllocs copies inputs, reads the result before release, and rolls back every prior allocation on failure. Focused tests cover each allocation failure/success path and a valid same-heap recovery.

See docs/step8-scalar-math.md.

routines.semantics: raw.convrt(value,inUnit,outUnit) calls actual CSPICE unit conversion with a finite scalar and unchanged unit strings; embedded NUL is rejected at the language/native boundaries. Supported angle, distance and time names/aliases use pinned N0067 conversion constants. Case and trailing blanks are accepted; leading blanks and unsupported singular spellings are not normalized by tspice. Empty, unknown and incompatible units preserve their genuine SPICE errors. NAIF requires callers to avoid floating overflow; the adapter retains numerical results without replacing historical estimates or adding a finite-output clamp.

scenarios.observes: Observe angular conversions including degrees/radians and hour/minute/second angle aliases.
Observe metric aliases and signed values across kilometer/meter/centimeter/millimeter scales.
Observe feet, inches, yards, statute miles and nautical miles through the pinned conversion table.
Observe AU, parsec, light-second and Julian light-year conversions using actual pinned constants; no modern astronomical constants are substituted.
Observe days, Julian years/YEARS, tropical years and hours/minutes/seconds, retaining their distinct conversion factors.
Observe mixed case and trailing blanks accepted by CSPICE without client-side string rewriting.
Observe zero, a negative scalar, and maximum finite scalar in an identity unit conversion.
Observe 1e200 and 1e-200 kilometer values converted to meters; focused actual-oracle rescaling makes tiny output observable.
Pass an unsupported input unit and observe UNITSNOTREC.
Pass an unsupported output unit and observe UNITSNOTREC.
Pass a leading-blank unit and observe UNITSNOTREC, preserving the distinction from accepted trailing blanks.
Pass METER and observe UNITSNOTREC instead of inventing a singular alias.
Convert distance to time and observe INCOMPATIBLEUNITS.
Pass an empty input-unit string and observe EMPTYSTRING from actual CSPICE.
Pass an empty output-unit string and observe EMPTYSTRING from actual CSPICE.

routines.semantics: raw.maxd(values) accepts a dense readonly array of finite doubles of length 0..30 and returns the actual CSPICE maximum. CSPICE tie/signed-zero selection is preserved rather than delegated to JavaScript Math.min/Math.max.
